summary: Fixed the typo: A_0 and A_1 each have measure half the circle; it is the same-phase gamma-RETURN SETS that are null, not A_i. Stopped re-checking the banked four-state field. Derived the exact AC-conditional finite filter: for a six-cycle, a same-direction group at direction d excludes the union of its cycle edges, so AC forbids it whenever that union covers >=4 of 6 labels. Verified the fixed q=(0,3,3,3,0,0) is excluded, in fact twice (d=0 and d=3, each union size 4; the d=3 group leaves {0,5} as the consumer note says). Then ran the single bounded process (0.02 s of 60 s): exhaustive enumeration of q in {0..5}^6 with q0=0, which is exactly one representative per rotation class. Result: 7776 candidates, 6356 fail AC, 1420 pass AC, and only 95 pass AC AND the six-orbit two-side constraints with palette cardinality <=2. So AC plus the orbit constraints cut the space by a factor 82 but do NOT eliminate it. A certificate is given for q=(0,0,1,3,3,4) with an explicit cyclic 3-palette assignment. Two exact reductions used: with six labels C4 kills all singletons, and the six phase cells are cyclic rotations so one check per q suffices.

conjectures: The 95 survivors are the obstacle: AC plus the six-orbit constraints are insufficient at the six-cycle stage, so a genuine F6 step needs a further source input. The survivors are the natural target for whatever comes next, and they should be published rather than searched further without a new constraint.

Because 95 of 1420 AC-passing configurations are orbit-feasible, AC is doing most of the filtering (82x total, 5.5x from AC alone to the orbit step). A strengthening that acts on same-direction groups with union size exactly 3 would bite hardest, since those are the groups AC just barely permits.

The survivor family contains genuine 3-palette orbit models, so any argument resting on 'two palettes per orbit' is already dead for q outside {0,3}^6 - a further reason the retracted claim was orbit-family-specific, not structural.

escalation.obstacle: Find a unit-distance graph with a genuine forced-equal distinct pair at k=5 (which by the corrected lemma requires chi>=5). Two seeds are now excluded by certificate. The open question is what structural feature makes the 5-colouring space rigid on a pair, given that richness of the colouring space defeated both seeds.
escalation.definitions: Unit-distance graph: finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. Forced equal at k: G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not; the added edge is a combinatorial disequality constraint and is never a unit edge for a non-adjacent pair. Coordinates in Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11), basis {1,3,5,11,15,33,55,165}, denominators dividing 288.
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; induced (all-pairs) edge set verified; k = 5; chi(G) >= 5 required for non-vacuity.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Common-neighbour palette excluders (Theorem B caps at 2 colours); clique-sum gluing (Theorem A); complete no-forcing certificates for H (553 vertices, 34 witnesses) and for H union (H+tau) (1048 vertices, 34 witnesses, 1048 unique signatures); adaptive equal-signature refinement driving survival sets to zero twice.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a forced-equal pair at k=5 with exact coordinates and a validated proof certificate, or a third seed that also resists, in which case the informative quantity is which invariant of the surviving classes differs between seeds; neither cross-edge count nor chromatic order has been shown to control rigidity.
